report.headline: Usage projected to jump from 19.5% to 23.9% in the EuroLeague, but the shooting-efficiency projection carries no information

projection.text: The model projects usage rate to rise to 23.9%, up from 19.5% in the 2010-11 NBA season and above the EuroLeague average of 20.3% (sd 4.4%).

risks.text: The true shooting projection of 54.7% carries no information: the model's error on true shooting (4.7%) is no better than simply guessing the EuroLeague average, and the bundle flags it as not to be trusted.

Source-season true shooting (51.5%) was already 0.52 standard deviations below the NBA average that season, and the true shooting slope of 0.536 implies only partial carry-over of relative standing even before accounting for the model's unreliability on this metric.

Players who actually made this NBA-to-EuroLeague move sat 0.31 standard deviations below their own league's average, not above it, so this transition should not be read as a star player switching leagues.
Source-season usage (19.5%) was itself 0.11 standard deviations below the NBA average, meaning the projected rise to 23.9% is built on a below-average NBA role rather than an above-average one.

strengths.text: Projected usage of 23.9% sits above the EuroLeague average of 20.3%, and the fitted slope of 0.986 for usage means a player's relative standing carries across the transition almost fully.

For usage rate the model beats the best trivial baseline (3.3% mean absolute error versus 4.3% for guessing the league mean), so the ranking implied by the usage projection is worth trusting even though the point estimate is not precise.
Assist rate (13.1%) and a low turnover rate (9.4%) in the source season describe a low-mistake, ball-involved profile heading into an expanded role.

uncertainty.text: The 80% prediction interval for usage runs from 19.5% to 28.4% and the 95% interval from 17.1% to 30.7% — a span of roughly two standard deviations of the EuroLeague usage distribution (sd 4.4%), so the model can say this is a more-featured role than the NBA one but cannot pin down how much more.
